title: Shareholder Litigation and Corporate Innovation
eligible_reason: Staggered adoption of universal demand (UD) laws by 23 states of incorporation (1989-2005); binary absorbing treatment `law`; firm-year panel 1977-2006 with firm FE and headquarters-state-by-year FE, clustered by incorporation state; several main-text columns have no controls. Caveat: the published paper's firm panel (firmpanel.dta, 942 firms = 471 treated + 471 never-treated controls, 19,096 firm-years) is a matched sample (abstract: 'Using a difference-in-differences design and a matched sample'); the regressions are plain TWFE on that sample, not pair-based matched DiD. Lead must decide whether the matched-sample restriction triggers the 'matching-based DiD' exclusion. State-level validity panel (Table 2B) is unmatched.
design_notes: Treatment `law` (label 'UD laws') = 1 once the firm's historical state of incorporation has a UD law. firmpanel.dta: 942 firms (gvkey_num), fyear 1977-2006, 19,096 rows; 471 firms ever treated across 13 first-treatment years (1989: 59, 1990: 50, 1991: 15, 1992: 62, 1993: 4, 1995: 24, 1996: 17, 1997: 162, 1998: 1, 2001: 1, 2003: 7, 2004: 65, 2005: 4), 471 never treated, 0 always-treated, no switch-off. FE: gvkey_num (firm) + state_year (label 'group(state_hist year)' = headquarters/operating state x year); cluster incorp_hist_id (historical incorporation state). Controls: ctrl1 = l1_ln_atw l1_levw l1_mbw l1_ln_age l1_roa; ctrl2 = l1_xrdf_atw + ctrl1 (all lagged firm-level, time-varying). Table 7 dynamics use d_3-d_1 d0-d2 d3x (t-3..t+3+, omitted t-4 and earlier) with controls. Table 9 interacts law with high/low litigation-risk and institutional-ownership groups. validity2.dta: 50 incorporation states x 1994-2013 (1,000 rows), law=1 for 388 state-years; 23 ever-treated states, 27 never; 9 states already treated in 1994 (always-treated within window); within-window adoption years 1995 (1), 1996 (2), 1997 (5), 1998 (1), 2001 (1), 2003 (1), 2004 (1), 2005 (2). Published PDF not accessible (HKU repositories blocked); the 2018 working paper (carloalberto.org) used an unmatched 57,310-obs sample, so its firm-level coefficients are not the published ones; its state-level Table 3B numbers are recorded as provisional values for Table 2B.

screener_notes: Package: ~/did_packages/mnsc/mnsc.2020.3626/data_program/ with estimate.do (all tables), figure_append.do (internet appendix figures), firmpanel.dta (firm panel), validity1.dta (duration model), validity2.dta (state-year validity panel). Underlying sources are licensed (Compustat, CRSP, patent data, Audit Analytics, Stanford SCAC) but the analysis datasets are shipped, so re-estimation is feasible. Key caveat: firmpanel.dta is a matched sample (variables treat, match_year; exactly 471 treated and 471 control firms); the abstract confirms 'a matched sample'. The regressions themselves are standard TWFE (firm FE + HQ-state x year FE) with staggered adoption across 13 cohorts, so CSA/BJS can be run on the same sample; lead to decide whether the matched-sample restriction falls under the 'matching-based DiD' exclusion. Published coefficients could not be retrieved (INFORMS paywalled; HKU repository DNS failure / 403); the 2018 WP is on a different, unmatched 57,310-obs sample, so only its state-level Table 3B values are carried over as provisional for Table 2B. Table 8 (added controls, two-way clustering, IHS outcomes) and Table 9 (law x high/low litigation risk and institutional ownership) are excluded (controls; subgroup-by-treatment interactions).
